The dividend is just part of the value.  The stocks themselves grow alongside the dividend.  You could have $100k sunk into dividends and make your 5% from those, but the stocks will grow about 7% in an average year as well so you get about 12%.

The comparison to a fixed $5 a year from a $100 Treasury really framed this well, especially the point that a bond payment never rises while groceries and health care keep getting more expensive. Paychex stood out to me: it only needs about 4.8% annual dividend growth to outpay the Treasury over the decade, yet its slowest growth over the past 1, 5, and 10 years was 10%. That cushion, plus 15 years of dividend raises, made the case much clearer than just chasing the highest yield.

I bought 100 shares of PAYX at the beginning of 2023.  Sold it in May of this year for a loss.  Yes, I received the dividend during that time frame, but it was not worth it.  Held it for over 3 years and lost money.  YMMV.  Good luck.
